title: Is the Shannon capacity of the 7-cycle below its Lovász theta?
credit: Lovász (1979) / Shannon (1956); status per Tao's optimization-constants list (2026)
premise_risks: Lower bound actively moving on Tao's list (2026, partly AI-produced and unrefereed); the posed question concerns the untouched upper side
plain: The Shannon capacity Θ(G) of a graph measures how many messages per channel use can be sent with zero error when G records which symbols can be confused. For the 7-cycle the best lower bound is about 3.2588 (2026 computer constructions) and the only upper bound is still Lovász's 1979 theta number 7cos(π/7)/(1+cos(π/7)) ≈ 3.3177. Decide whether Θ(C_7) is strictly smaller than this theta value.
math: For a graph $G$ let $\Theta(G)=\sup_{k\ge1}\alpha(G^{\boxtimes k})^{1/k}$, $\boxtimes$ the strong product. Decide whether $\Theta(C_7)<\vartheta(C_7)=\dfrac{7\cos(\pi/7)}{1+\cos(\pi/7)}$; equivalently (since $\Theta\le\vartheta$), whether $\Theta(C_7)=\vartheta(C_7)$ fails.
